v-heft.bottom_line: In men with chronic congestive heart failure on digoxin and a diuretic, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo reduced cumulative mortality at two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent; risk reduction 34 percent, P<0.028).
v-heft.implications: These results support a lower cumulative mortality with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo through two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) with an adjusted Cox-model mortality-risk reduction estimate of 34 percent (P<0.028; 95 percent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent), while prazosin showed no difference vs placebo. The document also notes that beyond three years the study had insufficient data for comparison and that full-dose persistence with hydralazine–isosorbide was limited (55 percent at six months).

v-heft-ii.bottom_line: In 804 men with chronic congestive heart failure receiving digoxin and diuretics, enalapril reduced two-year mortality to 18 percent vs 25 percent with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate (P = 0.016).
v-heft-ii.implications: The trial supports that, in this population and dosing, two-year mortality was lower with enalapril (18 percent) than with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate (25 percent; P = 0.016), with the difference attributed to fewer sudden deaths, while overall mortality over the full follow-up was not statistically significant (P = 0.08). It does not support concluding that enalapril improves peak oxygen consumption versus hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate, since oxygen consumption increased significantly only with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate early in follow-up, and it does not show a between-group difference in pump-failure mortality.

save.bottom_line: In patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction, captopril vs placebo reduced mortality from all causes by 19 percent (95 percent confidence interval, 3 to 32 percent; P = 0.019).
save.implications: Based on the reported event rates, this trial supports that, in this enrolled population, captopril was associated with lower all-cause mortality (19 percent risk reduction; 95 percent confidence interval, 3 to 32 percent) and lower risks of several major cardiovascular outcomes (e.g., cardiovascular death 21 percent; severe heart failure 37 percent; recurrent myocardial infarction 25 percent). The document also reports more frequent symptoms such as cough with captopril and higher discontinuation due to cough (27 vs 9). These numbers do not establish benefit or safety in patients outside the studied post–myocardial infarction group with ejection fraction of 40 percent or less and without overt heart failure or ischemic symptoms as enrolled here.

aire.bottom_line: In survivors of acute myocardial infarction with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality by 27% (95% CI 11% to 40%).
aire.implications: These data support that, in this selected post-AMI population with clinical evidence of heart failure, allocation to ramipril (vs placebo) was associated with lower all-cause mortality (170/ramipril vs 222/placebo; 27% risk reduction, 95% CI 11% to 40%) and a lower risk of the prespecified first validated composite outcome (19% reduction, 95% CI 5% to 31%). The document also reports more hypotension with ramipril (42 [4-2%] vs 23 [2-3%]) and does not provide evidence here to conclude a clear effect on reinfarction or stroke because event numbers were small.

woscops.bottom_line: In men with hypercholesterolemia and no history of myocardial infarction, pravastatin vs placebo reduced the risk of definite nonfatal MI or death from CHD by 31% (95% CI, 17 to 43 percent; P<0.001).

dig.bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction of 0.45 or less, digoxin vs placebo did not affect all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07).
dig.implications: These data support that, in the main trial, digoxin reduced hospitalization for worsening heart failure (26.8% vs 34.7%; risk ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.79) without reducing all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.91 to 1.07). The results also indicate a higher risk of hospitalization for suspected digoxin toxicity with digoxin (2.0% vs 0.9%; risk ratio, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.42 to 3.32).

rales.bottom_line: In RALES, spironolactone vs placebo reduced death from any cause (relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001).

The results also show increased serious hyperkalemia (5.5 percent vs 3.9 percent; P=0.002), so the findings do not establish net benefit without considering this reported safety tradeoff.

cards.bottom_line: In patients with type 2 diabetes without previous cardiovascular disease, atorvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo reduced major cardiovascular events (rate reduction 37% [95% CI –52 to –17], p=0.001).
cards.implications: In this population, atorvastatin 10 mg daily was associated with fewer first major cardiovascular events than placebo (127 vs 83; hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83]) and fewer strokes (0.52 [0.31–0.89]). Total mortality was lower numerically but not statistically significant (0.73 [0.52–1.01], p=0.059). These results support efficacy for reducing first major cardiovascular events over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, while the magnitude of any mortality effect remains uncertain based on the reported interval and p value.

prove-it-timi-22.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, the intensive regimen (2-year primary end point 22.4%) was associated with fewer primary end point events than the standard regimen (26.3%), with a reported 16 percent hazard reduction (95 percent confidence interval, 5 to 26 percent). The results also show different achieved LDL levels (median 62 vs 95 mg per deciliter) and more ALT elevations >3× ULN with high-dose atorvastatin (3.3% vs 1.1%); they do not establish the mechanism of benefit or isolate whether LDL lowering vs other differences between statins caused the outcome difference.

commit.implications: These results support that, during the scheduled in-hospital treatment period, metoprolol did not significantly reduce death (OR 0.99, 0.92–1.05) or the composite of death, reinfarction, or cardiac arrest (OR 0.96, 0.90–1.01), while it did reduce reinfarction (OR 0.82, 0.72–0.92) and ventricular fibrillation (OR 0.83, 0.75–0.93) but increased cardiogenic shock (OR 1.30, 1.19–1.41). criticisms.text: Bias for physician-initiated endpoints (eg, revascularization/unstable angina hospitalization) cannot be excluded due to open-label design.
criticisms.quote: the possibility of bias for some of the physician- initiated end points, such as coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina, cannot be excluded.

criticisms.text: Follow-up duration was shorter than anticipated in the protocol.
criticisms.quote: the follow-up duration was only a median of 4.8 years even though the study protocol anticipated the prespeci- fied number of primary end points to be reached after a median of 5.5 years.

criticisms.text: Primary endpoint did not reach statistical significance, possibly due to smaller-than-projected LDL-C difference and/or adherence differences.
criticisms.quote: One explanation might be insufficient dif- ference in levels of LDL-C between the groups since the observed difference was slightly smaller than projected.

criticisms.text: Higher discontinuations in atorvastatin group may reflect reporting bias given open-label design.
criticisms.quote: This difference may reflect real nontol- erance to a high dose of atorvastatin, but the possibility of reporting bias is pres- ent given the open-label design of the trial.

charisma.bottom_line: Clopidogrel plus aspirin, as compared with placebo plus aspirin, did not significantly reduce the primary end point (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22).
charisma.implications: In this broad high-risk population, the reported primary composite outcome did not differ significantly between clopidogrel plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22), while the principal secondary composite outcome was lower (relative risk, 0.92; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.86 to 0.995; P = 0.04) and bleeding was increased for moderate bleeding (relative risk, 1.62; 95 percent confidence interval, 1.27 to 2.08; P<0.001) with a non-significant increase in severe bleeding (P = 0.09).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in a broad high-risk population; clopidogrel 75 mg daily plus low-dose aspirin vs placebo plus low-dose aspirin; median follow-up 28 months.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 15,603 patients with either clinically evident cardiovascular disease or multiple risk factors to receive clopidogrel (75 mg per day) plus low-dose aspirin (75 to 162 mg per day) or placebo plus low-dose aspirin and followed them for a median of 28 months.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy outcome was not significantly different between groups (6.8% vs 7.3%).
major_points.quote: The rate of the primary efficacy end point was 6.8 percent with clopidogrel plus aspirin and 7.3 percent with placebo plus aspirin (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22).

major_points.text: Principal secondary composite end point was reduced with clopidogrel plus aspirin (16.7% vs 17.9%).
major_points.quote: The respective rate of the principal secondary efficacy end point, which included hospitalizations for ischemic events, was 16.7 percent and 17.9 percent (relative risk, 0.92; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.86 to 0.995; P = 0.04)

major_points.text: Severe bleeding was numerically higher with dual therapy (1.7% vs 1.3%), and moderate bleeding was higher (2.1% vs 1.3%).
major_points.quote: The rate of the primary safety end point (severe bleeding according to the GUSTO definition) was 1.7 percent in the clopidogrel group and 1.3 percent in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.25; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.61; P = 0.09).

mega-study.bottom_line: In MEGA, diet plus 10–20 mg pravastatin daily reduced coronary heart disease versus diet alone (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49–0.91).
mega-study.implications: These data support that, in this trial population, adding pravastatin to diet lowered the incidence of coronary heart disease versus diet alone (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49–0.91; 66 vs 101 events). The trial does not show a statistically significant reduction in stroke at end of study (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.57–1.21) or total mortality (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.51–1.01). Safety conclusions are limited to the reported finding of no between-group difference in malignant neoplasms or other serious adverse events.

major_points.quote: Methods In this prospective, randomised, open-labelled, blinded study, patients with hypercholesterolaemia (total cholesterol 5·69–6·98 mmol/L) and no history of coronary heart disease or stroke were randomly assigned diet or diet plus 10–20 mg pravastatin daily.

major_points.quote: Findings 3966 patients were randomly assigned to the diet group and 3866 to the diet plus pravastatin group. Mean follow-up was 5·3 years.

major_points.text: Coronary heart disease events were lower with diet plus pravastatin (66) than diet alone (101), HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.49–0.91).

corona.bottom_line: In older patients with systolic ischemic heart failure, rosuvastatin vs placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.02).
corona.implications: These data support that, over a median follow-up of 32.8 months, rosuvastatin lowered LDL cholesterol and hsCRP but did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in the primary composite endpoint (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.02; P = 0.12) or all-cause death (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.05; P = 0.31), while being associated with fewer cardiovascular hospitalizations (2193 vs 2564; P<0.001).

euridis-adonis.bottom_line: In the combined EURIDIS/ADONIS trials, dronedarone vs placebo reduced recurrence of atrial fibrillation at 12 months (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.87).

triton-timi-38-2007.bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes with scheduled percutaneous coronary intervention, prasugrel vs. clopidogrel reduced the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.90).
triton-timi-38-2007.implications: These data support that, in this ACS population scheduled for PCI, prasugrel lowered the composite ischemic end point versus clopidogrel (9.9% vs. 12.1%; hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.90) and reduced stent thrombosis (1.1% vs. 2.4%), but increased non–CABG-related TIMI major bleeding (2.4% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio, 1.32) and fatal TIMI major bleeding (0.4% vs. 0.1%). The document also reports that death from any cause was similar (3.0% vs. 3.2%; hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.78–1.16), so it does not establish a mortality difference between treatments.

major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 13,608 patients with moderate-to-high-risk acute coronary syndromes with sched- uled percutaneous coronary intervention to receive prasugrel ... or clopidogrel ... for 6 to 15 months.

andromeda.bottom_line: In patients with severe heart failure and left ventricular systolic dysfunction, dronedarone vs placebo increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio in the dronedarone group, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.07 to 4.25).
andromeda.implications: In this trial of severe heart failure with reduced left ventricular systolic function, the reported data support an early increase in all-cause mortality with dronedarone vs placebo (25/310 vs 12/317; HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.07 to 4.25), while the primary composite of death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure was not statistically different (HR 1.38, 95% CI 0.92 to 2.09). The confidence intervals do not exclude smaller or no differences for the composite endpoint, and the study was stopped early after 627 patients with a median follow-up of about 2 months.

ontarget.bottom_line: At a median follow-up of 56 months, the primary outcome occurred in 1412 patients in the ramipril group (16.5%), as compared with 1423 patients in the telmisartan group (16.7%; relative risk, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94 to 1.09).
ontarget.implications: Based on the reported primary outcome rates (16.7% vs. 16.5%) and relative risk (1.01; 95% CI, 0.94 to 1.09), the trial supports that telmisartan produced a similar primary composite outcome rate to ramipril within the study’s noninferiority framework; the CI does not support superiority of telmisartan over ramipril. Combination therapy showed no improvement in the primary outcome (relative risk, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.07) while showing higher adverse-event rates such as hypotensive symptoms (4.8% vs. 1.7%), syncope (0.3% vs. 0.2%), and renal dysfunction (13.5% vs. 10.2%).

athena.bottom_line: In 4628 patients with atrial fibrillation, dronedarone (400 mg twice a day) vs placebo reduced the primary outcome of first hospitalization due to cardiovascular events or death (hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.84).
athena.implications: These data support that, versus placebo, dronedarone reduced the composite of first hospitalization due to cardiovascular events or death (0.76, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.84; P<0.001) and reduced cardiovascular death (0.71, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.98; P=0.03), while not demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in all-cause death (0.84, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.08; P=0.18); bradycardia (3.5% vs 1.2%), QT-interval prolongation (1.7% vs 0.6%), diarrhea (9.7% vs 6.2%), nausea (5.3% vs 3.1%), rash (3.4% vs 2.0%) and serum creatinine increase (4.7% vs 1.3%) were more frequent with dronedarone.

major_points.text: Multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with atrial fibrillation and additional risk factors.
major_points.quote: ATHENA was a randomized, double- blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted accord- ing to the Declaration of Helsinki at 551 centers in 37 countries.

major_points.text: 4628 patients were randomized to dronedarone 400 mg twice daily or placebo.
major_points.quote: We conducted a multicenter trial to evaluate the use of dronedarone in 4628 patients with atrial fibrillation who had additional risk factors for death. Patients were ran- domly assigned to receive dronedarone, 400 mg twice a day, or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was first hospitalization due to cardiovascular events or death from any cause.
major_points.quote: The primary study outcome was the first hospi- talization due to cardiovascular events or death from any cause.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with dronedarone than placebo (HR 0.76, P<0.001).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 734 patients (31.9%) in the dronedarone group and in 917 patients (39.4%) in the placebo group, with a hazard ratio for drone- darone of 0.76 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.84; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Death from any cause was not significantly different between groups (HR 0.84; P=0.18).
major_points.quote: There were 116 deaths (5.0%) in the dronedarone group and 139 (6.0%) in the placebo group (haz- ard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.66 to 1.08; P = 0.18).

major_points.text: Death from cardiovascular causes was lower with dronedarone (HR 0.71; P=0.03).
major_points.quote: There were 63 deaths from cardiovas- cular causes (2.7%) in the dronedarone group and 90 (3.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.98; P = 0.03)

major_points.text: Deaths from cardiac arrhythmia were lower with dronedarone (HR 0.55; P=0.01).
major_points.quote: There were 26 deaths from cardiac arrhythmia (in 1.1% of patients) in the dronedarone group and 48 (in 2.1%) in the pla- cebo group (hazard ratio, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.34 to 0.88; P = 0.01)

major_points.text: Premature discontinuation of study drug was common and similar between groups (~30%).
major_points.quote: The mean follow-up period was 21±5 months, with the study drug discontinued prematurely in 696 of the 2301 patients (30.2%) receiving dronedarone and in 716 of the 2327 patients (30.8%) receiving placebo

major_points.text: Selected adverse events were more common with dronedarone, including bradycardia, QT prolongation, diarrhea, nausea, rash, and creatinine increase.
major_points.quote: Bradycardia, QT-interval pro- longation, diarrhea, nausea, rash, and an increase in the serum creatinine level were significantly more common in the dronedarone group than in the placebo group.

atlas-acs-timi-46.bottom_line: In patients stabilised after an acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban versus placebo increased clinically significant bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (hazard ratios [HRs] 2.21 [95% CI 1.25–3.91] for 5 mg, 3.35 [2.31–4.87] for 10 mg, 3.60 [2.32–5.58] for 15 mg, and 5.06 [3.45–7.42] for 20 mg doses; p<0.0001).
atlas-acs-timi-46.implications: These phase II data show that, compared with placebo, rivaroxaban increased clinically significant bleeding in a graded, dose-dependent manner (HRs 2.21 to 5.06 across 5–20 mg total daily doses; p<0.0001). The primary efficacy composite was not statistically different (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.60–1.05; p=0.10), while the main secondary composite (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) was lower with rivaroxaban (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.96; p=0.0270); the results support a possible reduction in major ischaemic outcomes but do not establish definitive benefit on the primary efficacy endpoint.

heaal.bottom_line: In patients with heart failure, reduced LVEF, and intolerance to ACE inhibitors, losartan 150 mg daily versus 50 mg daily reduced death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99).
heaal.implications: These data support that, in this ACE-inhibitor–intolerant heart failure population, losartan 150 mg daily yields a lower hazard of the composite of death or admission for heart failure than losartan 50 mg daily (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99) and a lower hazard of heart failure admission (HR 0.87, 0.76–0.98), while all-cause death was not significantly different (HR 0.94, 0.84–1.04). The results also show higher rates of renal impairment (454 vs 317), hypotension (203 vs 145), and hyperkalaemia (195 vs 131) with 150 mg, and they do not quantify benefit versus placebo.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind trial comparing losartan 150 mg vs 50 mg daily in heart failure with reduced LVEF and ACE-inhibitor intolerance.
major_points.quote: This double-blind trial was undertaken in 255 sites in 30 countries. 3846 patients with heart failure of New York Heart Association class II–IV, left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or less, and intolerance to angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors were randomly assigned to losartan 150 mg (n=1927) or 50 mg daily (n=1919).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was the composite of death or admission for heart failure; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was death or admission for heart failure. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint occurred less often with 150 mg vs 50 mg (HR 0.90) over median 4.7 years follow-up.
major_points.quote: With 4·7-year median follow-up in each group (IQR 3·7–5·5 for losartan 150 mg; 3·4–5·5 for losartan 50 mg), 828 (43%) patients in the 150 mg group versus 889 (46%) in the 50 mg group died or were admitted for heart failure (hazard ratio [HR] 0·90, 95% CI 0·82–0·99; p=0·027).

major_points.text: Heart failure admission was reduced with 150 mg vs 50 mg (HR 0.87), while all-cause death did not differ significantly.
major_points.quote: For the two primary endpoint components, 635 patients in the 150 mg group versus 665 in the 50 mg group died (HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·84–1·04; p=0·24), and 450 versus 503 patients were admitted for heart failure (0·87, 0·76–0·98; p=0·025).

major_points.text: Renal impairment, hypotension, and hyperkalaemia were more common with 150 mg than 50 mg, but discontinuations were not significantly increased.
major_points.quote: Renal impairment (n=454 vs 317), hypotension (203 vs 145), and hyperkalaemia (195 vs 131) were more common in the 150 mg group than in the 50 mg group, but these adverse events did not lead to signiﬁcantly more treatment discontinuations in the 150 mg group.

plato.bottom_line: In this trial, ticagrelor as compared with clopidogrel reduced the primary composite end point at 12 months (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 0.92).
plato.implications: These data support that, in this acute coronary syndrome population, ticagrelor had lower 12-month incidence of the composite of vascular death/MI/stroke than clopidogrel (9.8% vs. 11.7%; hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77 to 0.92) while overall major bleeding was not significantly different (11.6% vs. 11.2%; P = 0.43); however, non–CABG-related major bleeding was higher (4.5% vs. 3.8%; P = 0.03) and stroke alone was not significantly different (1.5% vs. 1.3%; P = 0.22).

major_points.text: Multicenter, double-blind randomized trial comparing ticagrelor vs clopidogrel in acute coronary syndrome patients.
major_points.quote: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized trial, we compared ticagrelor (180-mg loading dose, 90 mg twice daily thereafter) and clopidogrel (300-to-600-mg loading dose, 75 mg daily thereafter)

major_points.text: Primary composite end point (vascular death, MI, or stroke) was lower with ticagrelor at 12 months.
major_points.quote: At 12 months, the primary end point — a composite of death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke — had occurred in 9.8% of patients receiving ti- cagrelor as compared with 11.7% of those receiving clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 0.92; P<0.001).

major_points.text: No significant difference in overall major bleeding, but non–CABG-related major bleeding was higher with ticagrelor.
major_points.quote: No significant difference in the rates of major bleeding was found between the ticagrelor and clopidogrel groups (11.6% and 11.2%, respectively; P = 0.43), but ticagrelor was associated with a higher rate of major bleeding not re- lated to coronary-artery bypass grafting (4.5% vs. 3.8%, P = 0.03)

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with ticagrelor.
major_points.quote: The rate of death from any cause was also reduced with ticagrelor (4.5%, vs. 5.9% with clopid­ ogrel; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Stroke alone did not differ significantly between groups.
major_points.quote: but not stroke alone (1.5% vs. 1.3%, P = 0.22).

re-ly.bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation at risk for stroke, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily reduced stroke or systemic embolism versus warfarin (relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82).
re-ly.implications: These results support that, in this trial, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily had lower annual rates of stroke or systemic embolism than warfarin (1.11% per year vs 1.69% per year; relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82) with similar major bleeding (3.11% per year vs 3.36% per year; P = 0.31), while dabigatran 110 mg twice daily had similar stroke or systemic embolism (1.53% per year vs 1.69% per year; relative risk, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.11) and lower major bleeding (2.71% per year vs 3.36% per year; P = 0.003). The document also reports higher myocardial infarction rates with dabigatran than with warfarin and does not establish differences in mortality at conventional significance levels (e.g., P = 0.051 for dabigatran 150 mg vs warfarin).

current-oasis-7.bottom_line: In patients undergoing PCI, double-dose clopidogrel reduced cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke at 30 days versus standard-dose clopidogrel (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99).
current-oasis-7.implications: These 30-day PCI-subgroup results support that double-dose clopidogrel (vs standard-dose) was associated with a lower rate of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (3.9% vs 4.5%; adjusted HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74–0.99) and lower definite stent thrombosis (0.7% vs 1.3%; HR 0.54, 0.39–0.74), while increasing CURRENT-defined major bleeding (1.6% vs 1.1%; HR 1.41, 1.09–1.83). In the same PCI population, the trial does not show a difference between high-dose and low-dose aspirin for the primary outcome (4.1% vs 4.2%; HR 0.98, 0.84–1.13).

re-deem.bottom_line: Compared with placebo, dabigatran was associated with a dose-dependent increase in major or clinically relevant minor bleeding, with hazard ratio (HR) 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
re-deem.implications: In this phase II trial of patients with recent myocardial infarction on dual antiplatelet therapy, adding dabigatran increased major or clinically relevant minor bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (e.g., HR 4.27 [1.86, 9.81] for 150 mg vs placebo). The study also shows reduced coagulation activity as reflected by lower D-dimer at weeks 1 and 4 (about 37% and 45% lower vs placebo), while ischaemic event rates were low with minor numerical differences across groups (e.g., 3.8% placebo vs 3.0% at 110 mg for the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, or non-haemorrhagic stroke).

rocket-af.bottom_line: In patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96).
rocket-af.implications: These results support that rivaroxaban achieved noninferiority versus warfarin for stroke/systemic embolism in this moderate-to-high-risk nonvalvular atrial fibrillation population (per-protocol HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.96; intention-to-treat HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.03), while major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was similar (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.11) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs. 0.7% per year) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs. 0.5% per year) were lower with rivaroxaban; the intention-to-treat superiority test for the primary endpoint was not significant (P = 0.12).

atlas-acs-2-timi-51.implications: These data support that, versus placebo, adding rivaroxaban after a recent acute coronary syndrome reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96) while increasing TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs 0.2%), with no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs 0.2%, P = 0.66). trilogy-acs.implications: These data show no statistically significant reduction in the primary composite end point with prasugrel versus clopidogrel in patients <75 years (HR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.05; P=0.21). major_points.text: Prespecified recurrent-event analysis suggested lower risk with prasugrel in patients under 75 years (HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.72–1.00; P=0.04).

paradigm-hf.implications: In this trial, compared with enalapril, LCZ696 was associated with lower event rates for the primary composite (21.8% vs. 26.5%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.73–0.87), cardiovascular death (13.3% vs. 16.5%; hazard ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.71–0.89), and death from any cause (17.0% vs. 19.8%; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.76–0.93). The data also show more symptomatic hypotension with LCZ696 (14.0% vs. 9.2%) alongside less cough (11.3% vs. 14.3%) and fewer creatinine elevations ≥2.5 mg/dl (3.3% vs. 4.5%). These numbers support a conclusion of superiority for the prespecified outcomes in this studied population and do not, by themselves, establish effects in populations not meeting the trial’s entry/run-in requirements.

augustus.bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation and a recent acute coronary syndrome or PCI treated with a P2Y12 inhibitor, apixaban resulted in less ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81).
augustus.implications: Based on the reported 6-month outcomes, apixaban (vs vitamin K antagonist) was associated with a lower incidence of ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (10.5% vs. 14.7%; hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81) and a lower incidence of death or hospitalization (23.5% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.93), while the composite of death or ischemic events was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 0.93; 0.75–1.16). Aspirin (vs placebo) increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (16.1% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio, 1.89; 1.59–2.24), while death or hospitalization was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 1.08; 0.96–1.21) and death or ischemic events was not tested for superiority after a nonsignificant hierarchical result.

dapa-hf.bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and a reduced ejection fraction, dapagliflozin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85).
dapa-hf.implications: Based on the reported hazard ratio for the primary composite outcome (0.74; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.85) and the reported event proportions (16.3% vs. 21.2%) over a median of 18.2 months, the results support that dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death than placebo in this trial population; the report also shows lower cardiovascular death (0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98) and all-cause death (0.83; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.97). The document does not show a significant difference in the prespecified worsening renal function composite (0.71; 0.44 to 1.16).

east-afnet-4.bottom_line: In patients with early atrial fibrillation and cardiovascular conditions, early rhythm control vs usual care reduced the first primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.94).
east-afnet-4.implications: These data support that, in this population, early rhythm control was associated with a lower rate of the composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, or hospitalization with worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome (3.9 vs 5.0 per 100 person-years; hazard ratio, 0.79; 96% CI, 0.66 to 0.94) without a significant difference in annual nights spent in hospital (5.8±21.9 vs 5.1±15.5 days per year; P = 0.23). They also support that overall primary composite safety events were similar (16.6% vs 16.0%), while serious adverse events of special interest related to rhythm-control therapy were more frequent with early rhythm control (4.9% vs 1.4%).

emperor-reduced.implications: These data support that, over a median of 16 months, empagliflozin compared with placebo lowered the risk of the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.86) and lowered total heart-failure hospitalizations (hazard ratio 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85), while slowing eGFR decline (–0.55 vs. –2.28 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year, P<0.001).
